clue.text: Skill in character presentation

parts.note: characters here are written letters rather than people in a play, so the presenting skill is good handwriting

explanation.surface: An actor's talent for bringing a role to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character presentation' suggests acting; the characters are actually letters of the alphabet, set down neatly by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Penmanship is the art of handwriting, the craft of forming written characters well.

clue.text: One of three needed for a Baker Street problem

definitions.text: One of three needed for a Baker Street problem

parts.words: One of three needed for a Baker Street problem
parts.note: Sherlock Holmes of Baker Street called a hard case a three-smoke problem, needing that many bowlfuls of tobacco

explanation.surface: A puzzle set in Sherlock Holmes's London street needs three of something to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'The Red-Headed League' Holmes calls the case 'quite a three-pipe problem', meaning he must smoke three before solving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes measured a tough case by how many smokes of tobacco it took to think through.

clue.text: Card player overtaken by sleep — bit of a neck

indicators.note: the card player comes behind the sleep, as one runner is passed by another

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
E is East, one of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: A bridge player nods off at the table and slumps forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West, so a card player can be E.
explanation.definitionFit: The nape is the back part of the neck.

clue.text: Vital none should be overlooked

explanation.surface: Something essential, with every detail to be checked.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: if none should be overlooked, every one of them matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means of the greatest importance; when none may be missed, each and every one counts.

clue.text: No place for a mobile home in this Eastern inn

definitions.text: No place for a mobile home in this Eastern inn

parts.words: No place for a mobile home in this Eastern inn
parts.note: the longer word for an Eastern inn starts with a word for a mobile home; take that away and what remains is a shorter word for the same inn

explanation.surface: A roadside lodge in the East turns away travellers towing their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: A caravanserai is an Eastern inn for travelling caravans; with no 'caravan' (a mobile home, in British use), the inn is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is a resthouse for travellers in Persia, Turkey and neighbouring lands.

clue.text: Senior police officer has to check the other ranks?

parts.note: to inspect is to check or examine
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A senior officer must look over the junior soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British police an inspector ranks above a sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a rank of police officer above sergeant.

clue.text: This love of legs is immature

definitions.text: This love of legs is immature

parts.words: This love of legs is immature
parts.note: the word joins love to make the phrase for a teenager's crush, and it is also a part of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A fondness for shapely legs is childish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calf love' is puppy love, an immature infatuation; the calf is also the back of the leg below the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf love is youthful infatuation, and the calf is the fleshy rear part of the shin.

clue.text: Commissioned writer on the side perhaps

parts.note: an author is a writer

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word side may come out in some other form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer is paid to produce something on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commissioned' reads like a paid writer's job, but it is the definition: given official authority. 'perhaps' is the anagram signal, and 'on the' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorised means officially empowered or sanctioned, as a commissioned agent is.

clue.text: Girl accepts set arrangement for niche in church

indicators.note: the girl takes the rearranged letters into her middle

parts.note: Fenella is a girl's name

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of set are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman takes on a set of flowers to arrange for a church alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set arrangement' looks like flower-arranging; 'arrangement' is the anagram signal and 'accepts' the container. A fenestella is an obscure church term, fairly defined by 'niche in church'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fenestella is a small recess in a church wall, often by the altar, holding the piscina.

clue.text: Supplier has a ring redesigned to make available to all

indicators.note: something redesigned is remade in a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A supplier gets a ring remade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges SUPPLIER with A and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To popularise something is to bring it within reach and understanding of ordinary people.

clue.text: College point-to-point

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
N is north, another compass point

explanation.surface: A college hosts a horse race across country.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; here it is read as a compass point, TO, and another compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Batsmen in the tradition of Jackson …

definitions.text: Batsmen in the tradition of Jackson

parts.words: Batsmen in the tradition of Jackson
parts.note: the American Civil War general Thomas Jackson earned a nickname for standing firm like a wall, and dogged defensive cricketers share his name

explanation.surface: Cricketers who play like a famous Jackson, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson held his line immovably; in cricket a batsman who blocks and scores slowly is said to stonewall.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers who bat purely defensively, refusing risk, are known for blocking the bowling like a wall.

clue.text: Such a player has a good hand on either side of him

definitions.text: Such a player has a good hand on either side of him

parts.words: Such a player has a good hand on either side of him
parts.note: a good hand suggests a strong card holding or a skilled helper alongside, but means each of a player's own hands is equally skilled

explanation.surface: A card player is flanked by partners holding strong cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good hand' sounds like cards or capable teammates; the player simply uses left and right hands equally well.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone equally skilful with left and right hands is described this way.

clue.text: … bring on a tail-ender from time to time

parts.note: to occasion something is to bring it on or cause it

indicators.note: the ender of the word tail is its final letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a captain sometimes calls up a lower-order batsman to bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-ender' splits: the end of 'tail' gives L. In cricket a tail-ender is a weak batsman near the bottom of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasional describes what happens now and then, not regularly; the phrase is adverbial, the answer an adjective.

clue.text: It may shield us from what the butler saw

definitions.text: It may shield us from what the butler saw

parts.words: It may shield us from what the butler saw
parts.note: a heraldic shield is one sense; another is the small plate round a keyhole that stops a servant peeping through

explanation.surface: A screen protects our privacy from a nosy servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What the Butler Saw' was a British seaside peep-show machine; the answer is both a coat-of-arms shield and the cover over a keyhole.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is a shield bearing arms and also a plate fitted round a keyhole.

clue.text: Stew required — sea scout left to make it

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged to make the dish named first

explanation.surface: A young scout has been left to cook the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make it' rearranges SEASCOUT with L; 'required' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassoulet is a slow-cooked French casserole of beans, sausage and meat.

clue.text: Places where pictures of stars may be taken

definitions.text: Places where pictures of stars may be taken

parts.words: Places where pictures of stars may be taken
parts.note: stars suggests astronomy or celebrity portraits, but pictures are films, shot away from the studio

explanation.surface: Spots where photographers snap celebrities or the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: A film shot outside the studio is made 'on location'.
explanation.definitionFit: Film crews shoot scenes at real outdoor sites away from the studio, called by this name.

clue.text: Name river in report

parts.note: the Oise is a river in France

explanation.surface: A river is named in a report.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be a loud bang, and a bang is a loud sound.

clue.text: Head, ultra-modern, apparently has mature outlook

indicators.note: apparently means the letters are plainly visible in the words just before

explanation.surface: The head teacher, very up to date, seems to take a grown-up view.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'heAD ULTra'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being grown up means seeing things with a mature outlook; the clue's phrase stands for the adjective.

clue.text: Wright may produce this revolver

parts.note: a wright is a maker, and a maker of farm wagons turns out the round part that revolves; a revolver suggests a gun

explanation.surface: A gunsmith named Wright makes a pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wright' looks like a surname but means a craftsman, as in wheelwright or cartwright; the revolver is a rotating part, not a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon's spoked wheel turns round, and a cartwright builds wagons.

clue.text: How the moon behaves according to Juliet

definitions.text: How the moon behaves according to Juliet

parts.words: How the moon behaves according to Juliet
parts.note: in the balcony scene Juliet tells Romeo not to swear by the moon, which changes every month

explanation.surface: Juliet's view of the moon's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet says 'O, swear not by the moon, th' inconstant moon, That monthly changes in her circled orb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet calls the moon fickle because its shape keeps changing through the month.

clue.text: Tender scene say in Romeo & Juliet

explanation.surface: A loving moment in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' is the verb, to look after; the second definition points to Juliet's garrulous carer in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend the sick is to look after them; Juliet's old carer is a major role in the play.

clue.text: Cut the rising Chelsea sort?

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a Chelsea bun is a sort of sweet bun, so the clue's sort stands for the kind of bun

explanation.surface: A snobbish Chelsea type, socially climbing, ignores people.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea bun is a British spiral currant bun; 'rising' turns BUNS upwards to give the answer. The clue's singular 'sort' has to stand for the plural buns.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore or rebuff them pointedly.

clue.text: Trainer on foot

parts.note: trainer suggests a coach for athletes, but means the sports footwear, worn on the foot

explanation.surface: A coach who walks rather than rides.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a trainer is a sports shoe, called a sneaker in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a kind of footwear worn for sport.

clue.text: They sometimes have it in the House

definitions.text: They sometimes have it in the House

parts.words: They sometimes have it in the House
parts.note: after a Commons vote the Speaker announces which side has it, the votes against being one side

explanation.surface: Something certain people own at home now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons the Speaker declares 'the ayes have it' or the opposite when the votes against win.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the votes against a motion in Parliament.

clue.text: Where the Sun King was placed in history

definitions.text: Where the Sun King was placed in history

parts.words: Where the Sun King was placed in history
parts.note: Louis XIV of France was called the Sun King, and his place in the line of Louis is his number

explanation.surface: A historian asks where the French monarch ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun King was Louis XIV, so his place in the line of French Louises is his ordinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis XIV was the Sun King: his ordinal, his position in the sequence of that name.

clue.text: Cat identified by sound of course

indicators.note: by sound means the answer is heard as another word

parts.note: links are a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A cat is of course recognised by the noise it makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as an everyday phrase; it is the golf course, links, which is said like the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears and a short tail.

clue.text: Seeming sensible to change

indicators.note: change means the letters of the words before are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Appearing sensible enough to accept change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges SENSIBLE with TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or professed, as opposed to real.
